title: Edge scanline probes & attention-sink detection playbook
body:
Purpose and scope: This note defines a practical, repeatable detection and triage workflow for attention-sink style failures observed during long-context onboarding (8k / 32k / 128k). The approach emphasizes lightweight, deterministic probes we can run as part of model onboarding checks and nightly regression sweeps. It focuses on two classes: (A) retrieval-induced sink (when retrieved chunks anchor generation to stale context) and (B) positional/kv-erosion sink (when attention weights collapse to a small prefix or repeating tokens as context length grows).

Motivation: Across recent onboarding runs we occasionally see outputs that ignore fresh user instructions after a retrieval prefix or after a long prefix boundary. These are brittle for production workloads that interleave retrieval and fresh user prompts. Existing heuristics (token overlap, simple perplexity) catch some cases but miss subtle attention collapses where semantics drift gradually. We need a probe set + detection metrics that:
- run fast (minutes per model for 8k probes, tens of minutes for 128k ensemble)
- produce interpretable failure signatures for SRE/engineers
- minimize false positives so rollouts are not blocked by noisy signals

High-level detection workflow:
1) Prepare probe families (scanline, shuffle, watermark, prefix-swap). Each family targets a distinct failure mode.
2) Run probes across target lengths (8k, 32k, 128k) and model variants (fp16, q4_0, q4_1, quantized-L2).
3) Collect outputs + internal traces where available (kv-cache size, attention entropy per layer if runtime exposes it).
4) Compute a small suite of metrics and derive failure flags via threshold rules and trend analysis.
5) If flagged, run targeted diffs (prefix ablation, retrieval removal) to produce a deterministic regression ticket payload.

Probe family descriptions (concise):
- Scanline probes: Generate a long context that alternates short user queries with long system-level retrieval fragments. The idea is to expose periodic anchor points and see whether responses progressively degrade or stick to an earlier anchor. Typical template: [R1][Q1][R2][Q2]... where Rn are 512-1024 token retrieval snippets and Qn are 1-3 token user instructions.
- Shuffle probes: Identical prompts but shuffle the order of retrieved chunks before the final question. If output fidelity varies strongly with chunk order (beyond expected odds) that suggests brittle positional attention.
- Watermark chains: Insert low-entropy token chains (synthetic but model-safe) in retrieval chunks to detect leaks of anchor tokens and to measure attention concentration. Example watermark: a sequence of uncommon punctuation-token combos that do not alter semantics but increase detectability.
- Prefix-swap probes: Swap the last 1–2 retrieval chunks with unrelated text and measure output drift. This isolates whether the model uses immediate recent KV cache vs earlier global context.
- Truncation probes: Gradually truncate the tail of the context (drop last 1k/2k/4k tokens) and observe continuity metrics to assess truncation sensitivity.

Metrics we compute (explainable, low-cost):
- Anchor divergence (JS over top-20 token probs between baseline and probe): captures distributional shift caused by manipulations.
- Instruction retention score (binary pass rate over a set of 40 short directive prompts embedded at different offsets): measures whether simple directives are followed when placed near the end of long context.
- Top-k overlap drift (fraction of top-10 tokens shared across shuffles): low overlap indicates brittle retrieval dependence.
- Attention entropy sweep (if layer attn probs are available): compute median entropy across tokens in a window; large entropy collapse in later positions is a sink signal. If runtime does not expose per-layer attention, estimate via model-output concentration (top-1 probability mass curve).
- Perplexity delta over insertion points (Delta PPL when watermark inserted vs removed).

Flagging rules (initial thresholds, subject to tuning):
- A: Anchor divergence > 0.35 and instruction retention < 85% 
- B: Top-k overlap drift < 0.5 on shuffle family AND median attention entropy drop > 20% at tail positions
- C: PPL delta > +12% for watermark insertion compared to baseline
If any two of the above hold across two or more probe templates at the same length, mark as medium severity.

Regression triage steps once flagged: (fast checklist)
- Re-run deterministic seed across exact same host to rule out hardware nondeterminism.
- Run ablation: remove retrieval entirely and run same prompt; if issue disappears, tag as retrieval-bound. Attach both outputs to the ticket.
- Run prefix-swap and mirror-swap (swap retrieval positions) and compute top-k overlap matrix; attach matrix screenshot.
- If attention traces available, export per-layer entropy CSV for first 32 layers and plot heatmap.
- If quantized variant flagged, run fp16 baseline to check for quantization regression.

Sample minimal ticket template (to attach to MLINF backlog):
- Title: Attention-sink candidate on model-X (32k) during retrieval-heavy scanline probes
- Short repro: path + probe id + seed + commit (or model artifact id)
- Evidence: baseline output, flagged output, JS divergence values, instruction retention failures (line numbers), linked traces
- Suggested severity: medium
- First owner recommendation: run fp16 ablation, confirm retrieval removal test, attach delta files

Prompt set examples (short picks used in the harness):
- Directive probe (embedded at offsets): "Please summarize the last two sentences in one short bullet." (used to measure instruction retention).
- Factual-sanity probe: ask a question that requires only the most recent retrieval chunk (e.g., "What is the author of the paragraph directly above?").
- Ambiguity probe: ask a deliberate ambiguous question after several retrievals to test grounding.
- Non-semantics watermark: a 60-token syntactically-innocuous but low-entropy token chain used purely for detection, e.g. "|||α·§||:,/—" repeated in patterns.

Operational considerations:
- Runtime traces: the more internal signals we can capture (kv-cache hits, attention logits, head-wise sparsity), the faster the root cause. However do not stall the baseline onboarding flow—harness should run with _optional_ trace mode that only SRE/devs enable.
- Cost: keep probe corpus small (40–100 probes per length) and execute parallelized across a small pool (4–8 GPUs) to limit costs. Nightly regression can subset to known flake-prone probes.
- False positives: to reduce noise, require signals across probe families and across two seeds. Keep an allowlist for known model behaviors per-arch (e.g., some Llama2-derived models have benign top-k drift at very long contexts).

Example harness config (human-readable):
- lengths: [8192, 32768, 131072]
- families: [scanline, shuffle, watermark, truncation, prefix-swap]
- seeds: [42, 427]
- reports: JSON summary + human diff + optional traces archive

Next steps / runbook:
- Implement scanline/shuffle/watermark templates in rvw-probes repo (PR owner: Ravi).
- Add a nightly job that runs the 8k sweep against new model artifacts and posts a summarized report to #applied-ml-alerts (owner: Joanne).
- Pilot 32k/128k ensemble runs for the 3 most-frequently-used model variants for a week and tune thresholds (owner: Samir).

Open questions and risks:
- Are watermark chains safe for production retrieval (no accidental semantic leakage)? We need legal/PD review on using synthetic tokens inside customer retrievals (mitigation: use these probes only on internal staging retrieval corpora).
- How to surface attention-sink regressions to non-ML reviewers? Recommendation: produce a single-page exec-friendly visualization (top-k drift heatmap + instruction retention pass rate).
- Quantization interactions: some quantization schemes may amplify positional collapse—we should include quantization ablation in every flagged run.

Appendix: quick checklist for engineers when filing a regression ticket:
- [ ] List probe ids + seeds + model artifact id
- [ ] Upload baseline and flagged outputs (side-by-side)
- [ ] Run retrieval removal ablation and upload outputs
- [ ] If available, attach per-layer entropy CSV
- [ ] Suggest whether likely retrieval-bound / kv-erosion / quantization

This playbook is intentionally iterative. Keep the probe corpus growing (add new failure archetypes as we see them in production). For immediate action, implement the scanline and shuffle families first and add the watermark probes as an opt-in trace mode.

Notes to self: prioritize low-friction automation so that flagged runs create high-quality tickets automatically (including diffs and suggested triage steps) — otherwise humans will ignore noisy alerts.

-- Evelyn
